priceSnapshot.note: The morning report was written at 08:52 COT with spot at 77,294.9 and framed the tape as a range between the 76,422.3 shelf and the 78,258.6 high. Four hours later that framing is intact and NEITHER gate has fired. Spot is 77,410.8, up 115.9 points, and the whole session has traded inside 76,536.3 to 77,868.8 - a 1.74 percent band, against a 1H ATR of 971.1. The reduce trigger needed a settled 1H close below 76,422.3 and the lowest settled 1H close since the morning stamp is 76,730.1. The add trigger needed a settled 1H close above 78,258.6 and the highest is 77,474.5, some 784 points short. What HAS changed is the shape inside the range: the 13:00Z bar wicked to 76,222.2 and closed 77,256.4, and every hour since has held a higher low - 76,536.3, 77,166.6, 76,760.7, 77,182.3 - so the market is compressing upward against the range top rather than rolling over. The upper timeframes remain stretched: 4H RSI 94.31, daily RSI 85.59, spot 8.26 percent above the 4H EMA20 and 14.90 percent above the daily EMA20.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $76,222.2 - the low of the 13:00Z bar and the deepest point of the post-spike pullback. The shelf the morning report leaned on, 76,422.3, was wicked through on that bar and reclaimed inside the hour, so the honest structural line is now the wick low rather than the shelf. A settled CLOSE below it would mean the higher-low sequence of the last five hours has broken and the whole 76,222.2 to 78,258.6 range has failed downward. Be clear about the room: spot is 1,188.6 points above it and the 1H ATR is 971.1, so one ordinary hour reaches this level without meaning anything - which is exactly why the trigger is a settled close and not a touch. Below it the CoinGlass map offers 75,920 and 75,400, then thins badly until 73,830.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $78,258.6 - the high of the 10:00Z bar and the ceiling of every hour since the 79,515.7 spike was sold. This is unchanged from the morning report and it has still not fired: the best settled 1H close since is 77,474.5. Reclaiming it on a close would put 79,368.3 and the 79,515.7 high back in play. The caveat is also unchanged and is the reason this run only added a small tranche rather than a full one: the 48-hour Model 3 heatmap above spot shows only faint teal streaks near 77,930, 78,290 and 79,100, so a break up walks into unmapped air and has to be paid for with real spot demand rather than forced short covering.

decisionBox.changed: The stance moves from HOLD to a small ADD, and the size is the whole point. The morning run marked to market and did nothing, which was the right call at 08:52 because the wallet had just been trimmed twice inside fifteen minutes by two catch-up runs. Four hours later the picture has firmed rather than cracked: the range held, the lows are rising, aggregate open interest on CoinGlass is 139.12 billion USD and still up 4.40 percent on twenty-four hours, and the fresh OKX venue open interest reads 2,331,486,229 USD against the 2,202,440,192 the morning report could only quote from an eleven-hour-old cached body. The wallet, though, is 54 percent cash with only 0.0013355 BTC in the core, and a third consecutive no-op in a confirmed-inflow uptrend is a decision too, just an unexamined one. So this run puts 18 USDT of idle cash into the long-term spot core at 77,410.8 - about 15 percent of the dry powder, roughly 0.00023253 BTC. That is deliberately small. The case against going bigger has not weakened at all: 4H RSI is 94.31 and daily RSI 85.59, the two highest readings anywhere in this file; spot is 14.90 percent above the daily EMA20 at 67,370.5 and 7.91 percent above the daily EMA200 at 71,733.4; and the heaviest mapped liquidity on the whole 48-hour heatmap sits at roughly 68,950 and 67,900, more than 8,400 points BELOW. No futures this run either - a long from here needs a stop under 76,222.2, which is 1,188.6 points away against a 971.1 hourly ATR, and a short into four straight Farside inflow days totalling 1,610.3 million USD is an opinion rather than a trade. Roughly 105 USDT stays back for a genuine retest of 76,222.2 or 75,611.2.

liquidation.note: Faint teal streak on the 48-hour Model 3 heatmap, read from band brightness against the right-hand price axis. It is the last mapped level before 80,000 and it is thin - a speed bump, not a target.

Second faint streak sitting almost exactly on the 78,258.6 range top, laid down by the 10:00Z hour that made that high. Its presence is why a settled close above the range top is more likely to accelerate than to stall.
Nearest mapped band above spot, roughly 519 points away, and the only thing between the current price and the range ceiling. Low intensity: there is very little leverage stacked overhead.

Teal-green band running to the right edge of the map, so it is live rather than historical. It is the freshest layer on the chart, built by the five hours of shelf defence between 76,222.2 and 77,868.8, and it sits between spot and the structural low.
Band left by the 07:00Z consolidation that preceded the vertical hour. First real resting cluster under the range.
Thinner band just under the 75,611.2 invalidation. Not enough depth to stop a move on its own.

Band from the overnight 00:00Z to 02:00Z build. Between 75,400 and here the map is close to empty, which remains the single most important thing it says: there is a roughly 1,600-point hole under the invalidation.

The brightest band on the map, full yellow at the top of the intensity scale, and 8,460.8 points below spot. This is where the leverage added during the 63k-to-69k phase is stacked. Far too distant to be a session target, but it is where an unwind would actually stop, and it is the reason this run added 18 USDT rather than 60.
Second yellow band immediately under the 68,950 magnet. Together the two form the heaviest zone on the 48-hour map by a wide margin.

liquidityMagnet.source: CoinGlass Liquidation Heatmap Model 3 (Binance BTC/USDT perpetual, 48 hour), read via browser screenshot and zoom against the right-hand price axis; header aggregates read as exact text. Used as the fallback because the OKX /public/liquidation-orders feed returned fills stamped 2026-08-16 around 63,090, roughly 5.6 days old and 14,300 points away from spot, and was discarded under the freshness guard.
liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is DOWN and it is not close. Above spot there are three faint teal streaks and nothing heavier; below spot the bands step down 76,650, 75,920, 75,400, 73,830 and then the two extreme yellow magnets at 68,950 and 67,900. Read this as an asymmetry of consequence rather than a forecast: a break up is unopposed but unfunded by forced covering, while a break down has something real to fall toward. Reading a heatmap is qualitative for USD depth - the price levels and the header aggregates are solid, the per-band dollar figures are not, so none are quoted.

calibration.note: The prior report is 2026-08-21-morning, generated at 08:52:00-05:00 with spot at 77,294.9. Four hours and six minutes of tape later, NEITHER gate has fired. The reduce line at 76,422.3 required a settled 1H close below it and the lowest settled 1H close in the window is 76,730.1; the 13:00Z bar did wick to 76,222.2 but that wick printed at 13:30Z, BEFORE the morning stamp, and the bar closed 77,256.4 regardless. priorReduceFired is therefore FALSE. The add gate at 78,258.6 also has not fired - best settled close 77,474.5, some 784 points short. actingHelped is TRUE, and the credit needs to be stated narrowly because the honest margin is tiny. Morning marked to market and did nothing; spot is now 77,410.8, up 115.9 points or 0.15 percent, so the 0.0013355 BTC core gained about 0.15 USDT and the 123.36 USDT of cash earned nothing. Measured purely on price a full deployment would have been worth roughly 0.04 USDT more. That is noise. What earns the yes is the part of the decision that was NOT passive: morning explicitly declined to trim a third time inside the same quarter hour, and price went up rather than down, so refusing to churn was right. The lesson this run carries forward is the mirror image and it is the reason the stance changed. Morning was correct to sit still for one session; a THIRD consecutive no-op with the wallet 54 percent cash, the range holding, open interest rising and four days of confirmed ETF inflows would stop being patience and start being drift. The cost of that drift is not zero even though it does not show up in a snapshot.
